title: Pearl Atelier — Warm Boutique Consulting Glass
description: Warm pearl-and-platinum glass floating over a dim charcoal-teal field, framed by brushed champagne gold hairlines and anchored in serif display type. The anti-tech glass template — where cold cyan is a category error and every surface reads expensive.
philosophy: This template exists for rooms where trust is the product — private-client briefings, luxury-house strategy reviews, boutique consulting credentials presented across a mahogany table. It refuses the icy, tech-forward glass aesthetic that colonised SaaS decks, insisting instead on pearl warmth, champagne gold hairlines, and serif type that signals permanence over disruption. The charcoal-to-deep-teal background field holds quiet authority without collapsing into theatrical black-void drama. It is designed for speakers whose brand equity depends entirely on restraint.
goodFor: Luxury brand or fashion-house strategy presentations
Boutique consulting firm credential and case-study decks
Full-bleed hero slides carrying a single headline and one supporting stat
avoidFor: Chart-heavy quarterly reviews with dense multi-series data grids
Tech startup product demos or high-velocity investor day marathons
High-ambient-light conference halls where 0.5 px gold hairlines vanish
Multi-column infographic or newsletter-style information layouts
author: harness

examples.promptCore: Hushed luxury: a frosted pearl glass panel hovers above a deep charcoal-teal field with luminous, shadowless lift — the quiet authority of a private briefing room, not a stage. Compositional rhythm is deliberately asymmetric; the title anchors left-of-center with a single champagne gold hairline breathing below it, the right field left open and still. The overall feeling should be hand-pressed letterhead turned into architecture — permanent, legible across a mahogany table, never theatrical. Avoid icy cyan glow, neon edge-lit effects, hard drop shadows, or any kinetic energy; restraint is the identity.

examples.layoutNotes: 12-column grid with an 8% breathing outer margin; hero text occupies columns 1–7, left-aligned, with the right columns left as open dark field — no competing element. A single horizontal hairline rule sits beneath the title, spanning columns 1–5, and acts as the sole typographic separator between title and subtitle. A frosted glass panel rises from the lower-left quadrant, bleeding to roughly the two-thirds horizontal mark, layered at low z-order so the charcoal-teal background reads through its upper portion. Firm name or deck context is pinned bottom-right in the outer margin; no top header band.

examples.promptCore: The slide reads like a page extracted from a private-client brief — unhurried, curated, and implying consequence. A frosted pearl surface drifts slightly left of center, its warm translucency catching the dim teal-charcoal field behind it. Hairline rules act as quiet editorial punctuation between insight blocks, lending structure without rigidity. Avoid symmetrical grid cadence, icon rows, and any visual language that signals speed or volume over authority.

examples.layoutNotes: 12-column grid with a primary frosted glass panel anchored in cols 2–9, leaving the right edge open to the charcoal-teal field for compositional breathing. Content is structured as two or three insight blocks — each introduced by a short label and separated by a full-width champagne gold hairline rule rather than whitespace alone. A pull-stat or single-sentence finding occupies a typographically elevated moment at the top of the panel, with supporting detail below at reduced scale. Page folio sits bottom-right outside the panel; no persistent header band.
